entities.summary:
Simmias of Macedon (unknown - 329 BCE) was a Macedonian officer and a member of the royal family of Alexander the Great's officers. He was the son of Andromenes from Tymphaia and the brother of Attalus and Amyntas, and is believed to have served in the phalanx division under his brother Amyntas. At the Battle of Gaugamela, Simmias took command of his division and played a significant role in the battle, which was a decisive victory for Alexander. Following the battle, Simmias was accused, along with his brothers, of involvement in a plot to overthrow Alexander, but the charges were likely unfounded. Despite the accusations, Simmias remained a loyal officer and continued to serve Alexander until his death in 329 BCE.

Simmias' life and actions are significant because they provide insight into the inner workings of Alexander's empire and the dynamics of the royal family. His service in the phalanx division and his role in the Battle of Gaugamela demonstrate the importance of the Macedonian army in Alexander's conquests.

The legacy of Simmias can be seen in the continued influence of the Macedonian empire on the ancient world, particularly in the Hellenistic period. His involvement in Alexander's court and his role in the Battle of Gaugamela demonstrate the significance of the royal family in shaping the course of history.

The Battle of Gaugamela was a pivotal moment in the history of the ancient world, marking a decisive victory for Alexander and the beginning of the end of the Persian Empire.

Simmias' involvement in the plot to overthrow Alexander highlights the challenges faced by the royal family in maintaining power and stability in the face of internal dissent and external threats.
